1	# Otium — hackathon repo (project: Pitchlist)
2	
3	Several people, each with their own coding agent, work in this repo at once. `AGENTS.md` points to this
4	file, so every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) reads the same instructions.
5	
6	**Read this whole file before writing any code.** A human will tell you which agent you are:
7	**Agent A (Data & infra)**, **Agent B (Intelligence)** or **Agent C (Product)**.
8	Your tasks are in `TODO.md` under your letter. Do them in order, one short branch per task.
9	The full product write-up is in `OVERVIEW.md`.
10	
11	> Start prompt for humans:
12	> `Read CLAUDE.md and TODO.md. You are Agent A. Start with the first unchecked A-task.`
13	
14	## Project
15	
16	- **Theme:** Junction 2026 — Cala challenge "Make Unicorns Real": a product for founders/investors built on Cala's public data.
17	- **Idea:** Pitchlist — who's a fit, and who has a conflict, from either side of the table (details in §1).
18	- **Stack:** Python/FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, Cala, Gemini, MongoDB Atlas, Verda (details in §3).
19	- **Run:** set in task T1 — backend `uvicorn api.main:app --reload` from `backend/`; frontend `npm run dev` in `frontend/`. Update this line when T1 lands.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Entire (session tracking)
24	
25	This repo uses [Entire](https://docs.entire.io). Git hooks attach each agent session to a commit as a **checkpoint** (stored in git refs, synced to `origin` on push). That lets everyone see why code exists and what other agents already tried.
26	
27	- **Set this up once per clone:** `entire enable --agent <claude-code|codex|cursor|...>`. Git hooks are not cloned, so `entire status` shows "Enabled" even when nothing is being recorded. Check that `.git/hooks/post-commit` exists. If it doesn't, commits won't create checkpoints.
28	- For exact commands and flags, run `entire agent-help`; don't guess.
29	- **Before starting work**, see what others did: `entire checkpoint list`, `entire recap`, and `entire search "<topic>"`.
30	- **Before changing code you didn't write**, run `entire why <file>:<line>` or `entire checkpoint explain <sha>`.
31	- Don't commit `.entire/{tmp,metadata,logs}`; they are already gitignored. Don't edit `.claude/settings.json` hooks by hand.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Coordination rules
36	
37	The goal is to avoid merge conflicts. They come from long-lived branches and from several people editing the same files.
38	
39	1. **One branch per task, kept short.** Branch from fresh `main` (`git pull --rebase` first). Name it `<letter>/<task-id>-<slug>`, e.g. `a/A3-cala-client`. Merge back as soon as the task's tests pass (aim for under an hour), then delete the branch. Commit title starts with the task ID: `[A3] Cala client: retries + concurrency limit`. No PR review is needed unless you touch someone else's area. Never force-push `main`.
40	2. **Stay in your own directory.** Only edit files in the area you own (table below). If you need a change in someone else's area, don't make it: write the request in `notes/<your letter>.md` and tell your human.
41	3. **Change shared files in small, separate commits.** Dependency manifests (`backend/pyproject.toml`, `frontend/package.json`), `.env.example`, `TODO.md` ticks: minimal edit, own commit, push right away. Don't bundle with feature work.
42	4. **Contracts are frozen after task T2.** `contracts/` (schemas, API, fixtures format) changes only when all three humans agree. Then bump `CONTRACT_VERSION`, note it in `contracts/CHANGELOG.md`, and update §5 of this file **in the same commit**. Exception: Agent A writes fixture data into `contracts/fixtures/` (tasks A1, A2).
43	5. **Give each agent its own worktree.** If one person runs several agents, put each in its own git worktree (`git worktree add ../otium-<task> -b <branch>`). Never run two agents in the same folder.
44	6. **Commit small and often, with clear messages.** Each commit becomes an Entire checkpoint. Write one line saying what changed and why.
45	7. **Resolve conflicts using intent.** Run `entire why <file>:<line>` on both sides to see what each change was for, then keep both behaviours. Ask a human if the two can't both be kept.
46	8. **Ask a human before broad refactors**, renaming shared files, or reformatting the whole repo.
47	9. **Don't add a dependency** if a few lines of code would do. Never commit secrets; put them in `.env`, which must be gitignored. Only Agent A adds variable *names* to `.env.example`.
48	10. **Keep sources attached and use IDs.** Every fact you pass on keeps its `sources: list[Source]`. Use Cala entity IDs, never names, as keys (Cala has 5 different "Inventure"s).
49	11. **If a task is unclear or blocked, stop and ask your human.** Don't guess across someone else's area.
50	
51	### Definition of done (every task)
52	
53	- Code only in your area; contracts untouched.
54	- Tests for the new code pass (`pytest backend/tests/<your folder>` or `npm run build && npm test` in `frontend/`); `ruff` / `eslint` clean.
55	- Returns or serves contract models; sources preserved.
56	- Task ticked in `TODO.md` (your own line only) in a separate small commit.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Areas / owners
61	
62	| Path | Owner |
63	| --- | --- |
64	| `contracts/` | ALL — frozen after T2 (`contracts/fixtures/` data: A) |
65	| `backend/data/`, `backend/cache/`, `backend/batch/`, `deploy/`, `.env.example` | **A** — Data & infra |
66	| `backend/core/`, `backend/agent/`, `backend/mcp_server/`, `backend/api/` | **B** — Intelligence |
67	| `frontend/`, `docs/`, `README.md` | **C** — Product |
68	| `backend/tests/<folder>/` | owner of that folder |
69	| `notes/A.md`, `notes/B.md`, `notes/C.md` | that agent only |
70	| `CLAUDE.md`, `OVERVIEW.md`, `TODO.md` | humans (agents only tick their own TODO line) |
71	
72	### Repo layout
73	
74	```text
75	Otium/
76	  CLAUDE.md (AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md)   OVERVIEW.md   TODO.md   README.md (C)
77	  contracts/        schemas.py, api.md, CHANGELOG.md, fixtures/{raw,models}/*.json
78	  backend/
79	    pyproject.toml          shared manifest (rule 3)
80	    data/                   A  cala_client.py, store.py, fake_store.py, parsers.py, record_fixtures.py
81	    cache/                  A  atlas.py, vector.py
82	    batch/                  A  precompute_graph.py
83	    core/                   B  competitors.py, conflict.py, scoring.py, briefs.py
84	    agent/                  B  llm.py, gemini_agent.py, tools.py, prompts/
85	    mcp_server/             B  server.py
86	    api/                    B  main.py
87	    tests/                  data/ cache/ batch/ (A) · core/ agent/ mcp_server/ api/ (B)
88	  frontend/                 C  Next.js app, lib/types.ts, lib/api.ts, mock/
89	  deploy/                   A  Dockerfile, verda.md
90	  docs/                     C
91	  notes/                    A.md, B.md, C.md
92	```
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 1. What we are building
97	
98	**Pitchlist** — "who's a fit, and who has a conflict, from either side of the table." Slush starts right after the hackathon.
99	
100	- **Founder mode (main):** founder enters their company → we find its competitors in Cala → their funding rounds → the investors behind them → rank investors to **Pitch** and list investors to **Skip** (conflicts), each claim with a source.
101	- **Investor mode (the flip):** investor enters their fund + a startup → conflicts with their portfolio, the startup's competitors and who backed them, round history.
102	- **Slush prep agent:** paste the investors you're meeting → Gemini agent runs our tools → one sourced brief per investor.
103	- **MCP server:** the same functions exposed as MCP tools, so any agent (Claude Desktop, Cursor) can ask "should I pitch Fund X?".
104	
105	Conflict = an investor backed a direct competitor (`PORTFOLIO`), or one of its people sits on a competitor's board (`BOARD`).
106	
107	**Principle:** facts come only from Cala. Scoring is plain, deterministic code. The LLM (Gemini) only (1) judges which candidates are real competitors, (2) formats briefs from already-fetched sourced claims, (3) orchestrates tool calls in the agent/chat. The LLM never invents numbers, dates or investors.
108	
109	---
110

1	# Otium — hackathon repo (project: Pitchlist)
2	
3	Several people, each with their own coding agent, work in this repo at once. `AGENTS.md` points to this
4	file, so every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) reads the same instructions.
5	
6	**Read this whole file before writing any code.** You are one of three agents:
7	**Agent A (Data & infra)**, **Agent B (Intelligence)** or **Agent C (Product)**.
8	**Your role is in `CLAUDE.local.md`** in the repo root. That file is gitignored, so each clone has its own. If the file is missing, or your human gave you no role, ask your human before doing anything.
9	Your tasks are in `TODO.md` under your letter. Follow the **Task loop** and the **Gates** below.
10	The full product write-up is in `OVERVIEW.md`.
11	
12	> Setup for humans, once per clone: `echo "You are Agent B (Intelligence)." > CLAUDE.local.md`
13	> Then start each session with: `Read CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and TODO.md, then continue with my next task.`
14	
15	## Project
16	
17	- **Theme:** Junction 2026 — Cala challenge "Make Unicorns Real": a product for founders/investors built on Cala's public data.
18	- **Idea:** Pitchlist — who's a fit, and who has a conflict, from either side of the table (details in §1).
19	- **Stack:** Python/FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, Cala, Gemini, MongoDB Atlas, Verda (details in §3).
20	- **Setup (once per clone):** from the repo root, `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e "backend[dev]"` (Python 3.11+; this also makes `contracts` importable), then `cd frontend && npm install`. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have.
21	- **Run:** backend `uvicorn api.main:app --reload --env-file ../.env` from `backend/` (once B1 adds `api/main.py`); frontend `npm run dev` in `frontend/`.
22	- **Check:** `pytest backend/tests/<your folder>` and `ruff check backend contracts` from the repo root (venv active); `npm run build && npm run lint` in `frontend/`.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Entire (session tracking)
27	
28	This repo uses [Entire](https://docs.entire.io). Git hooks attach each agent session to a commit as a **checkpoint** (stored in git refs, synced to `origin` on push). That lets everyone see why code exists and what other agents already tried.
29	
30	- **Set this up once per clone:** `entire enable --agent <claude-code|codex|cursor|...>`. Git hooks are not cloned, so `entire status` shows "Enabled" even when nothing is being recorded. Check that `.git/hooks/post-commit` exists. If it doesn't, commits won't create checkpoints.
31	- For exact commands and flags, run `entire agent-help`; don't guess.
32	- **Before starting work**, see what others did: `entire checkpoint list`, `entire recap`, and `entire search "<topic>"`.
33	- **Before changing code you didn't write**, run `entire why <file>:<line>` or `entire checkpoint explain <sha>`.
34	- Don't commit `.entire/{tmp,metadata,logs}`; they are already gitignored. Don't edit `.claude/settings.json` hooks by hand.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Coordination rules
39	
40	The goal is to avoid merge conflicts. They come from long-lived branches and from several people editing the same files.
41	
42	1. **One branch per task, kept short.** Branch from fresh `main` (`git pull --rebase` first). Name it `<letter>/<task-id>-<slug>`, e.g. `a/A3-cala-client`. Merge back as soon as the task's tests pass (aim for under an hour), then delete the branch. Commit title starts with the task ID: `[A3] Cala client: retries + concurrency limit`. No PR review is needed unless you touch someone else's area. Never force-push `main`.
43	2. **Stay in your own directory.** Only edit files in the area you own (table below). If you need a change in someone else's area, don't make it: write the request in `notes/<your letter>.md` and tell your human.
44	3. **Change shared files in small, separate commits.** Dependency manifests (`backend/pyproject.toml`, `frontend/package.json`), `.env.example`, `TODO.md` ticks: minimal edit, own commit, push right away. Don't bundle with feature work.
45	4. **Contracts are frozen after task T2.** `contracts/` (schemas, API, fixtures format) changes only when all three humans agree. Then bump `CONTRACT_VERSION`, note it in `contracts/CHANGELOG.md`, and update §5 of this file **in the same commit**. Exception: Agent A writes fixture data into `contracts/fixtures/` (tasks A1, A2).
46	5. **Give each agent its own worktree.** If one person runs several agents, put each in its own git worktree (`git worktree add ../otium-<task> -b <branch>`). Never run two agents in the same folder.
47	6. **Commit small and often, with clear messages.** Each commit becomes an Entire checkpoint. Write one line saying what changed and why.
48	7. **Resolve conflicts using intent.** Run `entire why <file>:<line>` on both sides to see what each change was for, then keep both behaviours. Ask a human if the two can't both be kept.
49	8. **Ask a human before broad refactors**, renaming shared files, or reformatting the whole repo.
50	9. **Don't add a dependency** if a few lines of code would do. Never commit secrets; put them in `.env`, which must be gitignored. Only Agent A adds variable *names* to `.env.example`.
51	10. **Keep sources attached and use IDs.** Every fact you pass on keeps its `sources: list[Source]`. Use Cala entity IDs, never names, as keys (Cala has 5 different "Inventure"s).
52	11. **If a task is unclear or blocked, stop and ask your human.** Don't guess across someone else's area.
53	12. **An empty key in `.env` doesn't block you.** Build against fakes: `FakeDataStore`, a mocked Gemini client in tests, the frontend mock. Add one line to `notes/<your letter>.md` saying "<task>: not yet checked against live <service>", and do that live check once the key arrives. Only stop if the task can't be done without the real service (A1 needs `CALA_API_KEY`).
54	
55	### Task loop (every task, exactly like this)
56	
57	```sh
58	# 1. Start: fresh main, then pick the task
59	git switch main && git pull --rebase
60	git fetch origin 'refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'      # teammates' checkpoints
61	#    Next task = your first unchecked task in TODO.md whose `Needs:` are all [x] on main
62	#    and whose gate (table below) is open. If none is ready, tell your human what you're waiting for.
63	git switch -c b/B3-find-competitors                 # <letter>/<task-id>-<slug>
64	
65	# 2. Work: only in your folders, small commits titled "[B3] ..."
66	
67	# 3. Finish: once the definition of done (below) is met
68	git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main          # rerun your tests if anything new came in
69	git switch main && git pull --rebase
70	git merge --ff-only b/B3-find-competitors           # if it fails, main moved: go back to the branch and repeat step 3
71	git push origin main && git branch -d b/B3-find-competitors
72	
73	# 4. Tick: your own TODO.md line only, in its own commit
74	git add TODO.md && git commit -m "[B3] done" && git push origin main
75	```
76	
77	If a push is rejected: `git pull --rebase`, rerun your tests, push again. Never `--force`.
78	After ticking a task that opens a gate, **tell your human: "Gate Gx is open; tell the others to pull."**
79	
80	### Gates (when the others can continue)
81	
82	A gate is open when its task is ticked on `main`. To check: `git pull --rebase && grep -E '^- \[x\] \*\*A2 ' TODO.md` (replace A2 with the task that opens the gate).
83	
84	| Gate | Opened by | Open when | Unblocks | While waiting |
85	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
86	| **G0 Scaffold** | A (with all three) | T1 + T2 ticked | A1 (also needs T3), A3, A5 · B2 · C1, C4 | — |
87	| **G1 Fixtures** (CP1) | A | **A2** ticked: `contracts/fixtures/models/*.json` + `get_store()` returning `FakeDataStore` | B1, B3, B4 → rest of B on the fake store · C2 → C3, C5–C7 | A: only A1 → A2, nothing else first · B: B2 · C: C1, C4 |
88	| **G2 Real data** (CP2) | A | **A12** ticked: `USE_FAKE_STORE=false` works for one demo company | B9 | B: B8 and polish on the fake store · C: screens on the mock |
89	| **G3 Founder E2E** (CP3) | B | **B10** ticked: real `FounderReport`s for the 3 demo companies | C8 · A17 · B11–B15 | A: A13–A16 · C: C7, C9 on the mock |
90	
91	### Definition of done (every task)
92	
93	- Code only in your area; contracts untouched.
94	- Tests for the new code pass (`pytest backend/tests/<your folder>` or `npm run build && npm test` in `frontend/`); `ruff` / `eslint` clean.
95	- Returns or serves contract models; sources preserved.
96	- Task ticked in `TODO.md` (your own line only) in a separate small commit.
97	
98	---
99	
100	## Areas / owners
101	
102	| Path | Owner |
103	| --- | --- |
104	| `contracts/` | ALL — frozen after T2 (`contracts/fixtures/` data: A) |
105	| `backend/data/`, `backend/cache/`, `backend/batch/`, `deploy/`, `.env.example` | **A** — Data & infra |
106	| `backend/core/`, `backend/agent/`, `backend/mcp_server/`, `backend/api/` | **B** — Intelligence |
107	| `frontend/`, `docs/`, `README.md` | **C** — Product |
108	| `backend/tests/<folder>/` | owner of that folder |
109	| `notes/A.md`, `notes/B.md`, `notes/C.md` | that agent only |
110	| `CLAUDE.md`, `OVERVIEW.md`, `TODO.md` | humans (agents only tick their own TODO line) |
111	
112	### Repo layout
113	
114	```text
115	Otium/
116	  CLAUDE.md (AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md)   OVERVIEW.md   TODO.md   README.md (C)
117	  contracts/        schemas.py, api.md, CHANGELOG.md, fixtures/{raw,models}/*.json
118	  backend/
119	    pyproject.toml          shared manifest (rule 3)
120	    data/                   A  cala_client.py, store.py, fake_store.py, parsers.py, record_fixtures.py
121	    cache/                  A  atlas.py, vector.py
122	    batch/                  A  precompute_graph.py

124	    agent/                  B  llm.py, gemini_agent.py, tools.py, prompts/
125	    mcp_server/             B  server.py

127	    tests/                  data/ cache/ batch/ (A) · core/ agent/ mcp_server/ api/ (B)

134	---
135	
136	## 1. What we are building
137	
138	**Pitchlist** — "who's a fit, and who has a conflict, from either side of the table." Slush starts right after the hackathon.
139	
140	- **Founder mode (main):** founder enters their company → we find its competitors in Cala → their funding rounds → the investors behind them → rank investors to **Pitch** and list investors to **Skip** (conflicts), each claim with a source.
141	- **Investor mode (the flip):** investor enters their fund + a startup → conflicts with their portfolio, the startup's competitors and who backed them, round history.
142	- **Slush prep agent:** paste the investors you're meeting → Gemini agent runs our tools → one sourced brief per investor.
143	- **MCP server:** the same functions exposed as MCP tools, so any agent (Claude Desktop, Cursor) can ask "should I pitch Fund X?".
144	
145	Conflict = an investor backed a direct competitor (`PORTFOLIO`), or one of its people sits on a competitor's board (`BOARD`).
146	
147	**Principle:** facts come only from Cala. Scoring is plain, deterministic code. The LLM (Gemini) only (1) judges which candidates are real competitors, (2) formats briefs from already-fetched sourced claims, (3) orchestrates tool calls in the agent/chat. The LLM never invents numbers, dates or investors.
148	
149	---
150	
151	## 2. Integration checkpoints
152	
153	| When | What connects | Done when |
154	| --- | --- | --- |
155	| **CP1** Fri night | T1–T3 together, then A1–A2, B1, C1–C2 | `contracts/` merged; B and C run on fakes and mocks |
156	| Sat 11:00 | Cala workshop | Open questions answered |
157	| **CP2** Sat ~15:00 | A → B: real `DataStore` replaces the fake | B's eval set passes on live Cala data for 1 company |
158	| **CP3** Sat ~20:00 (HARD) | B → C: frontend points at the real API | Founder mode end to end on 3 demo companies with sources. If not: cut investor mode / agent / MCP down |
159	| **CP4** Sat night | Investor mode, Slush prep agent, MCP, batch job | Each works alone; then a joint smoke test |
160	| **CP5** Sun morning | Freeze → deploy on Verda → pre-cache → rehearse → submit | Demo runs from the deployed URL; backup video recorded |

164	## 3. Stack
165	
166	| Layer | Choice |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| Data | Cala REST API (+ Cala MCP for the demo) |
169	| LLM / agent | Gemini (API key provided). Flash-tier model for tool loops and competitor judging; Pro-tier only for brief formatting if quality requires |
170	| DB | MongoDB Atlas (cache by entity ID, precomputed graph, Atlas Vector Search) |
171	| Embeddings | Open-weight embedding model via Verda Inference API; Gemini embeddings as fallback |
172	| Precompute | Verda batch job (nightly) |
173	| Hosting | Verda CPU instance (backend + MCP server, Docker) |
174	| Backend | Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, httpx (async), official MCP Python SDK, pytest, ruff |
175	| Frontend | Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind |
176	| Not used | Tiger Data, GPU clusters, fine-tuning |

178	### Environment variables (`.env`, names owned by A)

196	
197	## 4. Cala — what we know (tested 13 Nov)
198	
199	- REST base `https://api.cala.ai/v1`, header `X-API-KEY: <key>`, `Content-Type: application/json`. Keys at console.cala.ai/api-keys; hackathon credits with promo code `MAKEUNICORNSREAL` (Billing → Extra credits).
200	  Exact query params/paths for the entity endpoints: **verify at docs.cala.ai/api-reference** before coding.
201	- `POST /knowledge/query` `{"input": "..."}` → structured rows + `entities[]` (IDs). Natural language or dot-notation: `companies.industry=X.country=Finland.funding_stage=Seed OR Series A.return(name, description, funding_stage, total_funding).limit=15`. Numbers come back as approximate strings ("~€15M", "over $100M").
202	- `POST /knowledge/search` `{"input": "..."}` → markdown answer + `explainability[]` (claim → reference IDs) + `context[]` (reference ID → source URL). Best source for "who led which round".
203	- Entity search by name (fuzzy, filter by entity type), entity lookup by LEI/CIK/etc., entity retrieval by UUID with a projection body `{"properties": [...], "relationships": {"outgoing": {"REL": {"limit": N}}, "incoming": {...}}}`, entity introspection (which fields/relationships exist for that entity).
204	- **Company** relationships: outgoing `OPERATES_IN_INDUSTRY`, `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `ISSUER`), `HAS_DOMAIN_NAME`; incoming `INVESTED_IN`, `IS_BOARD_MEMBER_OF`, `FOUNDED`, `IS_CEO_OF`, `WORKS_AT`. Properties incl. `funding_stage`, `total_funding`, `founding_date`, `headquarters_address`, `description`.
205	- **Investor** (Organization) relationships: outgoing `INVESTED_IN` (portfolio, sourced, **no dates**), `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `INVESTOR`, sometimes `is_lead: true` — sparse).
206	- **FundingRound** properties: `round_label`, `announcement_date`, `transaction_value`, `transaction_value_units`, `instrument`.
207	- Every property/relationship carries `sources[]` with `name`, `document` (URL), `date`, `source_rank` (`PRIMARY` | `FILING` | `PRESS` | `AGGREGATOR`; may be missing → `UNKNOWN`).
208	- Industry tags are coarse (all defence → `AEROSPACE_AND_DEFENSE`) → competitors need vector search + LLM judging.
209	- Known mismatch: "Inflection" (VC) resolved to Inflection AI → always check type + description for investors.
210	
211	Demo data: Kelluu (Series A, led by NATO Innovation Fund; also Keen Venture Partners, Gungnir Capital, Tesi). Maki.vc leads defence pre-seeds (Aavuus, Metaktik). Counter-drone set for a conflict demo: Sensofusion, Stendr, Nordic Air Defence.
212	
213	---
214	
215	## 5. Contracts (summary of `contracts/`; the files win if they differ)
216	
217	### 5.1 Models — `contracts/schemas.py`
218	
219	```python

321	### 5.2 Data layer interface — A implements, B consumes
322	
323	```python
324	class DataStore(Protocol):
325	    async def resolve(self, name: str, kind: Literal["company", "investor"]) -> list[EntityRef]: ...
326	    async def company(self, id: str) -> Company: ...
327	    async def rounds(self, company_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
328	    async def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
329	    async def portfolio(self, investor_id: str) -> list[PortfolioLink]: ...
330	    async def people(self, company_id: str) -> list[PersonLink]: ...
331	    async def candidate_competitors(self, company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Company]: ...
332	    async def co_investors(self, investor_id: str) -> list[tuple[EntityRef, int]]: ...
333	    async def sourced_answer(self, question: str) -> tuple[str, list[Reason]]: ...  # knowledge_search
334	```
335	
336	`backend/data/__init__.py` exposes `get_store() -> DataStore`, returning `FakeDataStore` when `USE_FAKE_STORE=true`, else the real store. B only ever calls `get_store()`.

338	### 5.3 REST API — B implements, C consumes
339	
340	| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
341	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
342	| POST | `/api/resolve` | `{name, kind}` | `EntityRef[]` |
343	| POST | `/api/founder/analyze` | `{company_id}` | `FounderReport` |
344	| POST | `/api/investor/check` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `InvestorCheck` |
345	| POST | `/api/brief` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `Brief` |
346	| POST | `/api/slush-prep` | `{company_id, investor_names: string[]}` | `{job_id}` |
347	| GET | `/api/jobs/{id}/stream` | — | SSE stream of `AgentEvent` |

353	### 5.4 MCP tools — B implements (thin wrappers over core)
354	
355	`resolve_company`, `find_competitors`, `get_rounds`, `investor_profile`, `check_conflict`, `rank_investors`, `investor_brief`. Inputs are entity IDs (plus `name` for `resolve_company`); outputs are the contract models as JSON.
356	
357	### 5.5 Fixtures — `contracts/fixtures/`
358	
359	- `raw/` — raw Cala responses (A records them; never hand-edited).
360	- `models/` — contract-model JSON built from raw (`company_<id>.json`, `rounds_<company_id>.json`, `portfolio_<investor_id>.json`, `founder_report_<company_id>.json`, ...).
361	- `FakeDataStore` reads `models/`. C's mock API serves `models/founder_report_*.json` etc.
362	
363	---
364	
365	## 6. Role briefs
366	
367	### Agent A — Data & infra
368	
369	You own the **only** code that talks to Cala, Atlas and Verda. Everything you return is a contract model with sources attached.
370	
371	- `cala_client.py`: async httpx client, `X-API-KEY`, retries with backoff, concurrency limit (semaphore, start at 8), timeout, log every call (endpoint, ms, cache hit) for credit tracking.
372	- `store.py`: `CalaDataStore` implementing `DataStore`. Map Cala JSON → models in small, tested mapper functions (one per model). Use introspection results to request only existing fields.
373	- `parsers.py`: amount text → EUR float (handle ~, over, M/B/K, $ / € / £ with a fixed FX table), partial dates → ISO prefix. Unparseable → `None`, never raise.
374	- Investor resolution: filter to Organization/Company types; prefer descriptions mentioning venture/capital/fund/invest.
375	- `cache/atlas.py`: wrap every Cala call — key = endpoint + entity ID or hash of input; TTL 24 h; `CACHE_ONLY=true` mode for the demo (no network).
376	- `cache/vector.py`: embed `name + description`; Atlas Vector Search index; `candidate_competitors` = top-k vector neighbours ∪ `knowledge_query` on same industry + Nordic/Baltic countries + adjacent stages; dedupe by ID; exclude the company itself.
377	- `batch/precompute_graph.py`: Verda batch job — list active Nordic/Baltic investors, fetch portfolios and rounds, write `investor_graph` (co-investor counts), `investor_activity` (last lead, rounds per sector/stage) and embeddings to Atlas. Idempotent, resumable, logs progress.
378	- `deploy/`: Dockerfile for the backend (API + MCP server), run instructions for a Verda CPU instance in `deploy/verda.md`.
379	
380	### Agent B — Intelligence
381	
382	You own the logic. Develop on `FakeDataStore` (`USE_FAKE_STORE=true`); never call Cala directly — always `get_store()`.
383	
384	- `core/competitors.py`: `find_competitors(company) -> list[Competitor]`. Get candidates from the store, ask Gemini (fast model, structured JSON output, temperature 0) to keep 10–15 direct competitors with a one-line reason each. Output may only contain candidate IDs (reject anything else).
385	- `core/conflict.py`: `check_conflict(investor_id, competitors) -> list[Conflict]`. PORTFOLIO = `portfolio(investor)` ∩ competitor IDs. BOARD = people of each competitor with role BOARD who are linked to the investor. Sources = union of the edges used.
386	- `core/scoring.py`: `rank_investors(company) -> FounderReport`. Investors = everyone in competitors' rounds. Signals: `leads_in_space`, `rounds_in_space`, recency of last lead, warm paths (`co_investors` overlap with the company's current investors). Any conflict → `skip`. Weights in one dict at the top of the file. Every number in `reasons` has sources.
387	- `core/briefs.py`: `investor_brief(investor_id, company_id) -> Brief`. Facts from store + `sourced_answer()`; Gemini only formats into one page; every sentence must map to a citation.
388	- `agent/`: Gemini function-calling loop over `tools.py` (core functions + `sourced_answer`). Max 12 tool calls per job, emits `AgentEvent`s. Powers slush-prep and chat.
389	- `mcp_server/server.py`: MCP tools from §5.4.
390	- `api/main.py`: routes exactly per §5.3, responses validated by the models, CORS, `/api/health`.
391	- Tests: `backend/tests/core/` with an eval set of known cases (TODO B8).
392	
393	### Agent C — Product
394	
395	You own what people see. Develop against `frontend/mock/` (fixture-based, same shapes as §5.3); switch to the real backend by setting `API_URL`.
396	
397	- TypeScript types in `frontend/lib/types.ts` mirror `contracts/schemas.py` exactly (same field names).
398	- One API client module `frontend/lib/api.ts`; components never call `fetch` directly.
399	- Screens: Home (mode toggle + entity resolve/confirm), Founder report (competitor chips, Pitch list, Skip list with conflict reason first), Investor brief, Investor check, Slush prep (paste list → live agent steps → brief cards), Chat panel.
400	- Every claim shows a **source badge**: rank (Primary / Filing / Press / Aggregator), date, link.
401	- States: loading, empty, error for every screen. Fast, clean, no clutter.
402	- `docs/` + `README.md`: setup, architecture, how Cala/Gemini/Atlas/Verda are used, demo script, pitch notes. Verda's judges require the process to be documented.
403

# Otium — hackathon repo (project: Pitchlist)

Several people, each with their own coding agent, work in this repo at once. `AGENTS.md` points to this
file, so every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) reads the same instructions.

**Read this whole file before writing any code.** You are one of three agents:
**Agent A (Data & infra)**, **Agent B (Intelligence)** or **Agent C (Product)**.
**Your role is in `CLAUDE.local.md`** in the repo root. That file is gitignored, so each clone has its own. If the file is missing, or your human gave you no role, ask your human before doing anything.
Your tasks are in `TODO.md` under your letter. Follow the **Task loop** and the **Gates** below.
The full product write-up is in `OVERVIEW.md`.

> Setup for humans, once per clone: `echo "You are Agent B (Intelligence)." > CLAUDE.local.md`
> Then start each session with: `Read CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and TODO.md, then continue with my next task.`

## Project

- **Theme:** Junction 2026 — Cala challenge "Make Unicorns Real": a product for founders/investors built on Cala's public data.
- **Idea:** Pitchlist — who's a fit, and who has a conflict, from either side of the table (details in §1).
- **Stack:** Python/FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, Cala, Gemini, MongoDB Atlas, Verda (details in §3).
- **Setup (once per clone):** from the repo root, `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e "backend[dev]"` (Python 3.11+; this also makes `contracts` importable), then `cd frontend && npm install`. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in what you have.
- **Run:** backend `uvicorn api.main:app --reload --env-file ../.env` from `backend/` (once B1 adds `api/main.py`); frontend `npm run dev` in `frontend/`.
- **Check:** `pytest backend/tests/<your folder>` and `ruff check backend contracts` from the repo root (venv active); `npm run build && npm run lint` in `frontend/`.

---

## Entire (session tracking)

This repo uses [Entire](https://docs.entire.io). Git hooks attach each agent session to a commit as a **checkpoint** (stored in git refs, synced to `origin` on push). That lets everyone see why code exists and what other agents already tried.

- **Set this up once per clone:** `entire enable --agent <claude-code|codex|cursor|...>`. Git hooks are not cloned, so `entire status` shows "Enabled" even when nothing is being recorded. Check that `.git/hooks/post-commit` exists. If it doesn't, commits won't create checkpoints.
- For exact commands and flags, run `entire agent-help`; don't guess.
- **Before starting work**, see what others did: `entire checkpoint list`, `entire recap`, and `entire search "<topic>"`.
- **Before changing code you didn't write**, run `entire why <file>:<line>` or `entire checkpoint explain <sha>`.
- Don't commit `.entire/{tmp,metadata,logs}`; they are already gitignored. Don't edit `.claude/settings.json` hooks by hand.

---

## Coordination rules

The goal is to avoid merge conflicts. They come from long-lived branches and from several people editing the same files.

1. **One branch per task, kept short.** Branch from fresh `main` (`git pull --rebase` first). Name it `<letter>/<task-id>-<slug>`, e.g. `a/A3-cala-client`. Merge back as soon as the task's tests pass (aim for under an hour), then delete the branch. Commit title starts with the task ID: `[A3] Cala client: retries + concurrency limit`. No PR review is needed unless you touch someone else's area. Never force-push `main`.
2. **Stay in your own directory.** Only edit files in the area you own (table below). If you need a change in someone else's area, don't make it: write the request in `notes/<your letter>.md` and tell your human.
3. **Change shared files in small, separate commits.** Dependency manifests (`backend/pyproject.toml`, `frontend/package.json`), `.env.example`, `TODO.md` ticks: minimal edit, own commit, push right away. Don't bundle with feature work.
4. **Contracts are frozen after task T2.** `contracts/` (schemas, API, fixtures format) changes only when all three humans agree. Then bump `CONTRACT_VERSION`, note it in `contracts/CHANGELOG.md`, and update §5 of this file **in the same commit**. Exception: Agent A writes fixture data into `contracts/fixtures/` (tasks A1, A2).
5. **Give each agent its own worktree.** If one person runs several agents, put each in its own git worktree (`git worktree add ../otium-<task> -b <branch>`). Never run two agents in the same folder.
6. **Commit small and often, with clear messages.** Each commit becomes an Entire checkpoint. Write one line saying what changed and why.
7. **Resolve conflicts using intent.** Run `entire why <file>:<line>` on both sides to see what each change was for, then keep both behaviours. Ask a human if the two can't both be kept.
8. **Ask a human before broad refactors**, renaming shared files, or reformatting the whole repo.
9. **Don't add a dependency** if a few lines of code would do. Never commit secrets; put them in `.env`, which must be gitignored. Only Agent A adds variable *names* to `.env.example`.
10. **Keep sources attached and use IDs.** Every fact you pass on keeps its `sources: list[Source]`. Use Cala entity IDs, never names, as keys (Cala has 5 different "Inventure"s).
11. **If a task is unclear or blocked, stop and ask your human.** Don't guess across someone else's area.
12. **An empty key in `.env` doesn't block you.** Build against fakes: `FakeDataStore`, a mocked Gemini client in tests, the frontend mock. Add one line to `notes/<your letter>.md` saying "<task>: not yet checked against live <service>", and do that live check once the key arrives. Only stop if the task can't be done without the real service (A1 needs `CALA_API_KEY`).

### Task loop (every task, exactly like this)

```sh
# 1. Start: fresh main, then pick the task
git switch main && git pull --rebase
git fetch origin 'refs/entire/*:refs/entire/*'      # teammates' checkpoints
#    Next task = your first unchecked task in TODO.md whose `Needs:` are all [x] on main
#    and whose gate (table below) is open. If none is ready, tell your human what you're waiting for.
git switch -c b/B3-find-competitors                 # <letter>/<task-id>-<slug>

# 2. Work: only in your folders, small commits titled "[B3] ..."

# 3. Finish: once the definition of done (below) is met
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main          # rerun your tests if anything new came in
git switch main && git pull --rebase
git merge --ff-only b/B3-find-competitors           # if it fails, main moved: go back to the branch and repeat step 3
git push origin main && git branch -d b/B3-find-competitors

# 4. Tick: your own TODO.md line only, in its own commit
git add TODO.md && git commit -m "[B3] done" && git push origin main
```

If a push is rejected: `git pull --rebase`, rerun your tests, push again. Never `--force`.
After ticking a task that opens a gate, **tell your human: "Gate Gx is open; tell the others to pull."**

### Gates (when the others can continue)

A gate is open when its task is ticked on `main`. To check: `git pull --rebase && grep -E '^- \[x\] \*\*A2 ' TODO.md` (replace A2 with the task that opens the gate).

| Gate | Opened by | Open when | Unblocks | While waiting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **G0 Scaffold** | A (with all three) | T1 + T2 ticked | A1 (also needs T3), A3, A5 · B2 · C1, C4 | — |
| **G1 Fixtures** (CP1) | A | **A2** ticked: `contracts/fixtures/models/*.json` + `get_store()` returning `FakeDataStore` | B1, B3, B4 → rest of B on the fake store · C2 → C3, C5–C7 | A: only A1 → A2, nothing else first · B: B2 · C: C1, C4 |
| **G2 Real data** (CP2) | A | **A12** ticked: `USE_FAKE_STORE=false` works for one demo company | B9 | B: B8 and polish on the fake store · C: screens on the mock |
| **G3 Founder E2E** (CP3) | B | **B10** ticked: real `FounderReport`s for the 3 demo companies | C8 · A17 · B11–B15 | A: A13–A16 · C: C7, C9 on the mock |

### Definition of done (every task)

- Code only in your area; contracts untouched.
- Tests for the new code pass (`pytest backend/tests/<your folder>` or `npm run build && npm test` in `frontend/`); `ruff` / `eslint` clean.
- Returns or serves contract models; sources preserved.
- Task ticked in `TODO.md` (your own line only) in a separate small commit.

---

## Areas / owners

| Path | Owner |
| --- | --- |
| `contracts/` | ALL — frozen after T2 (`contracts/fixtures/` data: A) |
| `backend/data/`, `backend/cache/`, `backend/batch/`, `deploy/`, `.env.example` | **A** — Data & infra |
| `backend/core/`, `backend/agent/`, `backend/mcp_server/`, `backend/api/` | **B** — Intelligence |
| `frontend/`, `docs/`, `README.md` | **C** — Product |
| `backend/tests/<folder>/` | owner of that folder |
| `notes/A.md`, `notes/B.md`, `notes/C.md` | that agent only |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `OVERVIEW.md`, `TODO.md` | humans (agents only tick their own TODO line) |

### Repo layout

```text
Otium/
  CLAUDE.md (AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md)   OVERVIEW.md   TODO.md   README.md (C)
  contracts/        schemas.py, api.md, CHANGELOG.md, fixtures/{raw,models}/*.json
  backend/
    pyproject.toml          shared manifest (rule 3)
    data/                   A  cala_client.py, store.py, fake_store.py, parsers.py, record_fixtures.py
    cache/                  A  atlas.py, vector.py
    batch/                  A  precompute_graph.py
    core/                   B  competitors.py, conflict.py, scoring.py, briefs.py
    agent/                  B  llm.py, gemini_agent.py, tools.py, prompts/
    mcp_server/             B  server.py
    api/                    B  main.py
    tests/                  data/ cache/ batch/ (A) · core/ agent/ mcp_server/ api/ (B)
  frontend/                 C  Next.js app, lib/types.ts, lib/api.ts, mock/
  deploy/                   A  Dockerfile, verda.md
  docs/                     C
  notes/                    A.md, B.md, C.md
```

---

## 1. What we are building

**Pitchlist** — "who's a fit, and who has a conflict, from either side of the table." Slush starts right after the hackathon.

- **Founder mode (main):** founder enters their company → we find its competitors in Cala → their funding rounds → the investors behind them → rank investors to **Pitch** and list investors to **Skip** (conflicts), each claim with a source.
- **Investor mode (the flip):** investor enters their fund + a startup → conflicts with their portfolio, the startup's competitors and who backed them, round history.
- **Slush prep agent:** paste the investors you're meeting → Gemini agent runs our tools → one sourced brief per investor.
- **MCP server:** the same functions exposed as MCP tools, so any agent (Claude Desktop, Cursor) can ask "should I pitch Fund X?".

Conflict = an investor backed a direct competitor (`PORTFOLIO`), or one of its people sits on a competitor's board (`BOARD`).

**Principle:** facts come only from Cala. Scoring is plain, deterministic code. The LLM (Gemini) only (1) judges which candidates are real competitors, (2) formats briefs from already-fetched sourced claims, (3) orchestrates tool calls in the agent/chat. The LLM never invents numbers, dates or investors.

---

## 2. Integration checkpoints

| When | What connects | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CP1** Fri night | T1–T3 together, then A1–A2, B1, C1–C2 | `contracts/` merged; B and C run on fakes and mocks |
| Sat 11:00 | Cala workshop | Open questions answered |
| **CP2** Sat ~15:00 | A → B: real `DataStore` replaces the fake | B's eval set passes on live Cala data for 1 company |
| **CP3** Sat ~20:00 (HARD) | B → C: frontend points at the real API | Founder mode end to end on 3 demo companies with sources. If not: cut investor mode / agent / MCP down |
| **CP4** Sat night | Investor mode, Slush prep agent, MCP, batch job | Each works alone; then a joint smoke test |
| **CP5** Sun morning | Freeze → deploy on Verda → pre-cache → rehearse → submit | Demo runs from the deployed URL; backup video recorded |

---

## 3. Stack

| Layer | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Data | Cala REST API (+ Cala MCP for the demo) |
| LLM / agent | Gemini (API key provided). Flash-tier model for tool loops and competitor judging; Pro-tier only for brief formatting if quality requires |
| DB | MongoDB Atlas (cache by entity ID, precomputed graph, Atlas Vector Search) |
| Embeddings | Open-weight embedding model via Verda Inference API; Gemini embeddings as fallback |
| Precompute | Verda batch job (nightly) |
| Hosting | Verda CPU instance (backend + MCP server, Docker) |
| Backend | Python 3.11+, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, httpx (async), official MCP Python SDK, pytest, ruff |
| Frontend | Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind |
| Not used | Tiger Data, GPU clusters, fine-tuning |

### Environment variables (`.env`, names owned by A)

```text
CALA_API_KEY=
CALA_BASE_URL=https://api.cala.ai/v1
GEMINI_API_KEY=
GEMINI_MODEL_FAST=          # Flash-tier model id
GEMINI_MODEL_SMART=         # Pro-tier model id (optional)
MONGODB_URI=
MONGODB_DB=pitchlist
VERDA_API_KEY=
VERDA_EMBED_MODEL=
USE_FAKE_STORE=true         # B and C develop on fixtures until the real store is ready (CP2)
CACHE_ONLY=false            # true = demo runs from the Atlas cache with no Cala calls
API_URL=http://localhost:8000   # frontend → backend; C's mock runs on another port
```

---

## 4. Cala — what we know (tested 13 Nov)

- REST base `https://api.cala.ai/v1`, header `X-API-KEY: <key>`, `Content-Type: application/json`. Keys at console.cala.ai/api-keys; hackathon credits with promo code `MAKEUNICORNSREAL` (Billing → Extra credits).
  Exact query params/paths for the entity endpoints: **verify at docs.cala.ai/api-reference** before coding.
- `POST /knowledge/query` `{"input": "..."}` → structured rows + `entities[]` (IDs). Natural language or dot-notation: `companies.industry=X.country=Finland.funding_stage=Seed OR Series A.return(name, description, funding_stage, total_funding).limit=15`. Numbers come back as approximate strings ("~€15M", "over $100M").
- `POST /knowledge/search` `{"input": "..."}` → markdown answer + `explainability[]` (claim → reference IDs) + `context[]` (reference ID → source URL). Best source for "who led which round".
- Entity search by name (fuzzy, filter by entity type), entity lookup by LEI/CIK/etc., entity retrieval by UUID with a projection body `{"properties": [...], "relationships": {"outgoing": {"REL": {"limit": N}}, "incoming": {...}}}`, entity introspection (which fields/relationships exist for that entity).
- **Company** relationships: outgoing `OPERATES_IN_INDUSTRY`, `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `ISSUER`), `HAS_DOMAIN_NAME`; incoming `INVESTED_IN`, `IS_BOARD_MEMBER_OF`, `FOUNDED`, `IS_CEO_OF`, `WORKS_AT`. Properties incl. `funding_stage`, `total_funding`, `founding_date`, `headquarters_address`, `description`.
- **Investor** (Organization) relationships: outgoing `INVESTED_IN` (portfolio, sourced, **no dates**), `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` (role `INVESTOR`, sometimes `is_lead: true` — sparse).
- **FundingRound** properties: `round_label`, `announcement_date`, `transaction_value`, `transaction_value_units`, `instrument`.
- Every property/relationship carries `sources[]` with `name`, `document` (URL), `date`, `source_rank` (`PRIMARY` | `FILING` | `PRESS` | `AGGREGATOR`; may be missing → `UNKNOWN`).
- Industry tags are coarse (all defence → `AEROSPACE_AND_DEFENSE`) → competitors need vector search + LLM judging.
- Known mismatch: "Inflection" (VC) resolved to Inflection AI → always check type + description for investors.

Demo data: Kelluu (Series A, led by NATO Innovation Fund; also Keen Venture Partners, Gungnir Capital, Tesi). Maki.vc leads defence pre-seeds (Aavuus, Metaktik). Counter-drone set for a conflict demo: Sensofusion, Stendr, Nordic Air Defence.

---

## 5. Contracts (summary of `contracts/`; the files win if they differ)

### 5.1 Models — `contracts/schemas.py`

```python
from typing import Literal, Protocol
from pydantic import BaseModel

CONTRACT_VERSION = "1.0.0"

SourceRank = Literal["PRIMARY", "FILING", "PRESS", "AGGREGATOR", "UNKNOWN"]

class Source(BaseModel):
    name: str
    url: str | None = None
    date: str | None = None          # ISO date or partial ("2025-10")
    rank: SourceRank = "UNKNOWN"

class EntityRef(BaseModel):
    id: str                          # Cala UUID
    name: str
    type: str                        # Company | Organization | Person | FundingRound ...
    description: str | None = None

class Company(EntityRef):
    industries: list[str] = []
    stage: str | None = None
    country: str | None = None
    total_funding_text: str | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []

class RoundInvestor(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    is_lead: bool | None = None      # None = unknown

class Round(BaseModel):
    id: str
    company_id: str
    label: str | None = None         # "Seed", "Series A" ...
    date: str | None = None
    amount_text: str | None = None
    amount_eur: float | None = None
    investors: list[RoundInvestor] = []
    sources: list[Source] = []

class PortfolioLink(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company: EntityRef
    sources: list[Source] = []

class PersonLink(BaseModel):
    person: EntityRef
    company_id: str
    role: Literal["BOARD", "FOUNDER", "CEO", "EMPLOYEE"]
    sources: list[Source] = []

class Competitor(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    reason: str
    similarity: float | None = None

class Conflict(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["PORTFOLIO", "BOARD"]
    competitor: EntityRef
    via_person: EntityRef | None = None
    sources: list[Source] = []

class Reason(BaseModel):
    text: str
    sources: list[Source] = []

class InvestorScore(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    score: float
    conflict: Conflict | None = None
    leads_in_space: int = 0
    rounds_in_space: int = 0
    last_lead_date: str | None = None
    warm_paths: list[Reason] = []
    reasons: list[Reason] = []

class FounderReport(BaseModel):
    company: Company
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    pitch: list[InvestorScore]
    skip: list[InvestorScore]

class InvestorCheck(BaseModel):
    investor: EntityRef
    company: Company
    conflicts: list[Conflict]
    competitors: list[Competitor]
    rounds: list[Round]

class Brief(BaseModel):
    investor_id: str
    company_id: str
    markdown: str
    citations: list[Source]

class AgentEvent(BaseModel):          # streamed by /api/jobs/{id}/stream and /api/chat
    type: Literal["step", "brief", "error", "done"]
    message: str | None = None
    brief: Brief | None = None
```

### 5.2 Data layer interface — A implements, B consumes

```python
class DataStore(Protocol):
    async def resolve(self, name: str, kind: Literal["company", "investor"]) -> list[EntityRef]: ...
    async def company(self, id: str) -> Company: ...
    async def rounds(self, company_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def portfolio(self, investor_id: str) -> list[PortfolioLink]: ...
    async def people(self, company_id: str) -> list[PersonLink]: ...
    async def candidate_competitors(self, company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Company]: ...
    async def co_investors(self, investor_id: str) -> list[tuple[EntityRef, int]]: ...
    async def sourced_answer(self, question: str) -> tuple[str, list[Reason]]: ...  # knowledge_search
```

`backend/data/__init__.py` exposes `get_store() -> DataStore`, returning `FakeDataStore` when `USE_FAKE_STORE=true`, else the real store. B only ever calls `get_store()`.

### 5.3 REST API — B implements, C consumes

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/resolve` | `{name, kind}` | `EntityRef[]` |
| POST | `/api/founder/analyze` | `{company_id}` | `FounderReport` |
| POST | `/api/investor/check` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `InvestorCheck` |
| POST | `/api/brief` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `Brief` |
| POST | `/api/slush-prep` | `{company_id, investor_names: string[]}` | `{job_id}` |
| GET | `/api/jobs/{id}/stream` | — | SSE stream of `AgentEvent` |
| POST | `/api/chat` | `{company_id?, investor_id?, message}` | SSE stream of `AgentEvent` (type `step` = text chunks) |
| GET | `/api/health` | — | `{ok: true, contract_version}` |

Errors: HTTP 4xx/5xx with `{error: string}`. CORS open for the frontend origin.

### 5.4 MCP tools — B implements (thin wrappers over core)

`resolve_company`, `find_competitors`, `get_rounds`, `investor_profile`, `check_conflict`, `rank_investors`, `investor_brief`. Inputs are entity IDs (plus `name` for `resolve_company`); outputs are the contract models as JSON.

### 5.5 Fixtures — `contracts/fixtures/`

- `raw/` — raw Cala responses (A records them; never hand-edited).
- `models/` — contract-model JSON built from raw (`company_<id>.json`, `rounds_<company_id>.json`, `portfolio_<investor_id>.json`, `founder_report_<company_id>.json`, ...).
- `FakeDataStore` reads `models/`. C's mock API serves `models/founder_report_*.json` etc.

---

## 6. Role briefs

### Agent A — Data & infra

You own the **only** code that talks to Cala, Atlas and Verda. Everything you return is a contract model with sources attached.

- `cala_client.py`: async httpx client, `X-API-KEY`, retries with backoff, concurrency limit (semaphore, start at 8), timeout, log every call (endpoint, ms, cache hit) for credit tracking.
- `store.py`: `CalaDataStore` implementing `DataStore`. Map Cala JSON → models in small, tested mapper functions (one per model). Use introspection results to request only existing fields.
- `parsers.py`: amount text → EUR float (handle ~, over, M/B/K, $ / € / £ with a fixed FX table), partial dates → ISO prefix. Unparseable → `None`, never raise.
- Investor resolution: filter to Organization/Company types; prefer descriptions mentioning venture/capital/fund/invest.
- `cache/atlas.py`: wrap every Cala call — key = endpoint + entity ID or hash of input; TTL 24 h; `CACHE_ONLY=true` mode for the demo (no network).
- `cache/vector.py`: embed `name + description`; Atlas Vector Search index; `candidate_competitors` = top-k vector neighbours ∪ `knowledge_query` on same industry + Nordic/Baltic countries + adjacent stages; dedupe by ID; exclude the company itself.
- `batch/precompute_graph.py`: Verda batch job — list active Nordic/Baltic investors, fetch portfolios and rounds, write `investor_graph` (co-investor counts), `investor_activity` (last lead, rounds per sector/stage) and embeddings to Atlas. Idempotent, resumable, logs progress.
- `deploy/`: Dockerfile for the backend (API + MCP server), run instructions for a Verda CPU instance in `deploy/verda.md`.

### Agent B — Intelligence

You own the logic. Develop on `FakeDataStore` (`USE_FAKE_STORE=true`); never call Cala directly — always `get_store()`.

- `core/competitors.py`: `find_competitors(company) -> list[Competitor]`. Get candidates from the store, ask Gemini (fast model, structured JSON output, temperature 0) to keep 10–15 direct competitors with a one-line reason each. Output may only contain candidate IDs (reject anything else).
- `core/conflict.py`: `check_conflict(investor_id, competitors) -> list[Conflict]`. PORTFOLIO = `portfolio(investor)` ∩ competitor IDs. BOARD = people of each competitor with role BOARD who are linked to the investor. Sources = union of the edges used.
- `core/scoring.py`: `rank_investors(company) -> FounderReport`. Investors = everyone in competitors' rounds. Signals: `leads_in_space`, `rounds_in_space`, recency of last lead, warm paths (`co_investors` overlap with the company's current investors). Any conflict → `skip`. Weights in one dict at the top of the file. Every number in `reasons` has sources.
- `core/briefs.py`: `investor_brief(investor_id, company_id) -> Brief`. Facts from store + `sourced_answer()`; Gemini only formats into one page; every sentence must map to a citation.
- `agent/`: Gemini function-calling loop over `tools.py` (core functions + `sourced_answer`). Max 12 tool calls per job, emits `AgentEvent`s. Powers slush-prep and chat.
- `mcp_server/server.py`: MCP tools from §5.4.
- `api/main.py`: routes exactly per §5.3, responses validated by the models, CORS, `/api/health`.
- Tests: `backend/tests/core/` with an eval set of known cases (TODO B8).

### Agent C — Product

You own what people see. Develop against `frontend/mock/` (fixture-based, same shapes as §5.3); switch to the real backend by setting `API_URL`.

- TypeScript types in `frontend/lib/types.ts` mirror `contracts/schemas.py` exactly (same field names).
- One API client module `frontend/lib/api.ts`; components never call `fetch` directly.
- Screens: Home (mode toggle + entity resolve/confirm), Founder report (competitor chips, Pitch list, Skip list with conflict reason first), Investor brief, Investor check, Slush prep (paste list → live agent steps → brief cards), Chat panel.
- Every claim shows a **source badge**: rank (Primary / Filing / Press / Aggregator), date, link.
- States: loading, empty, error for every screen. Fast, clean, no clutter.
- `docs/` + `README.md`: setup, architecture, how Cala/Gemini/Atlas/Verda are used, demo script, pitch notes. Verda's judges require the process to be documented.

1	# Pitchlist — Project Overview
2	
3	Nov 13, 2026 · @Atis Dubrovskis
4	
5	## The idea
6	
7	**Pitchlist tells you who's a fit and who has a conflict, from either side of the table.** It's a web app plus an MCP server, built on Cala's connected, sourced data on companies, funding rounds and investors.
8	
9	**The problem.** Founders build investor lists from logo walls and gut feeling, then waste weeks on three kinds of investor who were never going to say yes:
10	
11	- **Funds that don't lead.** They join rounds but rarely set the terms.
12	- **Funds that have gone quiet.** No new lead in 12+ months, and the fund is near the end of its life.
13	- **Funds with a conflict.** They already backed a direct competitor, so pitching them means handing your deck to a rival's board member.
14	
15	Investors have the mirror problem. At Slush they meet 30+ startups in two days and need to know fast whether a startup competes with their portfolio and who has backed its rivals.
16	
17	**Why Cala.** Spotting a conflict means walking the graph: company → competitors → rounds → investors → back to you. Web search can't do that reliably. Cala's connected, sourced data can, and every claim we show links to its source.
18	
19	## Users and modes
20	
21	One product with a toggle, "I'm raising / I'm investing," running on one engine. **Founder mode is the main product; investor mode is the flip.**
22	
23	|  | Founder mode (main) | Investor mode (the flip) |
24	| --- | --- | --- |
25	| User | Seed or Series A founder about to raise, e.g. at Slush | Angel, VC associate or partner screening deals |
26	| Input | My company | My fund plus a startup that pitched me |
27	| Question | Who should I pitch, and who should I skip? | Is this a fit, does it conflict with my portfolio, and who backed its rivals? |
28	| Output | Ranked investor list, a "don't pitch" list with reasons, a one-page brief per investor | One-screen check: conflict flags, market map, round history |
29	| Slush use | Paste the investors you're meeting, get prep briefs | Paste a startup between meetings, get a 60-second check |
30	
31	**Out of scope:** accounts, matching, messaging, anything that needs both sides active at once. It's not a marketplace.
32	
33	## How it works
34	
35	It's a fixed pipeline that calls Cala directly, so it's fast, gives the same answer every time, and can trace every claim to its source. The LLM is used in only two steps: judging who counts as a competitor, and writing the briefs. Every number comes from Cala, and the scoring is plain code.
36	
37	**Founder mode**
38	
39	1. **Resolve the company.** `entity_search` by name, confirm with the user if there's more than one match, then `retrieve_entity` for sector, stage, location and description.
40	2. **Find competitors.** `knowledge_query` for companies in the same sector, stage and region. *LLM step:* read the descriptions and keep 10–15 direct competitors, with a one-line reason for each.
41	3. **Pull their rounds.** One `knowledge_query` per competitor, in parallel: date, amount, investors, and whether each investor led. Cache everything.
42	4. **Check each investor's activity.** For the top investors, query their recent rounds: when they last led, in which sectors, at what stage.
43	5. **Score them** in code (see Scoring).
44	6. **Write the briefs.** *LLM step:* a one-page brief per investor, written only from the rows already fetched, with a source on every claim. Use `knowledge_search` (sourced prose) for small gaps.
45	
46	**Investor mode** runs the same steps from the other side. Step 1 resolves the fund and the startup. Step 2 finds the startup's competitors. The fund's portfolio is then compared with that competitor set: any overlap is a conflict, and steps 3–4 build the market map and round history.
47	
48	**Rule:** every data row keeps its Cala source link from fetch to UI, so any claim can show its source in one click.
49	
50	## Architecture
51	
52	[embedded content: architecture · 2 entry points, 1 core, Cala underneath\]
53	
54	The web app and the MCP server call the same core functions. Data flows from the data layer to scoring to the Gemini steps. Every Cala response is cached in Atlas, and a nightly Verda batch job precomputes the Nordic investor graph so demo lookups are instant.
55	
56	### Stack
57	
58	| Layer | Choice | Why |
59	| --- | --- | --- |
60	| Data source | Cala (REST API + MCP) | Sourced graph of companies, rounds, investors and people; the core of the product |
61	| Agent / LLM | Gemini (provided keys): a Flash-tier model for the tool loop and competitor judging, a Pro-tier model for briefs only if quality needs it | Strong function calling, fast and cheap for multi-step loops |
62	| Database | MongoDB Atlas | Cala returns JSON, so cache it as documents keyed by entity ID; Atlas Vector Search finds the closest companies to yours (competitor candidates) |
63	| Embeddings | Open-weight embedding model on Verda Inference API (or Gemini embeddings as fallback) | Vectors for company descriptions |
64	| Precompute | Verda batch job, nightly | Crawls every active Nordic and Baltic investor's portfolio from Cala, builds the co-investor graph, activity stats and embeddings ahead of time |
65	| Hosting | Verda CPU instance | Runs the FastAPI backend and the MCP server; gives a believable path from demo to real users |
66	| Backend | Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, official MCP Python SDK | One language for data, scoring, agent and MCP |
67	| Frontend | Next.js + Tailwind | Fast to build, easy to deploy |
68	| Not used | Tiger Data, Verda GPU clusters, fine-tuning | No real need; forcing them in hurts focus (and Verda's "Fit" score) |
69	
70	### How we use Cala
71	
72	**Graph for structure, search for narrative, IDs everywhere.** Each Cala feature has one job:
73	
74	| Cala feature | Its job in Pitchlist |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| `entity_search` | Resolve names to entity IDs; the user confirms when several match (there are 5 "Inventure"s) |
77	| `entity_introspection` | Run once per entity type at startup and cache which fields and relationships exist; never request fields blind |
78	| `entity_retrieval` with relationship projections | The backbone. `INVESTED_IN` for portfolios and conflicts, `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` for rounds and `is_lead`, `IS_BOARD_MEMBER_OF` / `FOUNDED` / `WORKS_AT` for board-seat conflicts and warm paths |
79	| `knowledge_query` (dot-notation) | Discovery: candidate competitors and recent rounds by industry, country and stage. Its `entities[]` IDs feed straight into `entity_retrieval` (query first, then walk the graph) |
80	| `knowledge_search` | Fills gaps the graph is thin on (who led, how recently). Its `explainability` claims plus their references are shown as citations as-is, not rewritten by the LLM |
81	| Source metadata | Every claim shows a source badge built from `source_rank` (PRIMARY / FILING / PRESS / AGGREGATOR) and date; prefer primary sources when facts conflict |
82	
83	**What this lets us show that web search can't:** conflicts several hops away (competitor → investor → partner → board seat), co-investor warm paths, and how reliable each claim is.
84	
85	## Scoring
86	
87	An investor's score is the sum of four signals, and a conflict overrides the score. All of it is plain code with readable reasons, and the weights are a first guess to tune on real data on Saturday.
88	
89	| Signal | What it measures | Shown as |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Conflict | Backed a direct competitor (founder mode) or holds one (investor mode); or its partner sits on a competitor's board | Hard flag → "Don't pitch" list, with the competitor and a source |
92	| Leads in your space | Share of their rounds in your sector and stage where they led | "Led 4 of 6 fintech seeds" |
93	| Still active | Months since their last lead; number of new deals in the last 12 months | "Last lead: Mar 2026" |
94	| Warm path | Co-invested with your existing investors, or backs founders you know | "Co-invested with Inventure 3×" |
95	
96	If Cala doesn't mark lead investors, "leads in your space" falls back to how often they appear in your space at all, and the UI says so.
97	
98	## MCP tools
99	
100	The web app and the MCP server call the same functions. Any agent (Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT) can ask "Should I pitch Fund X?", and the answer comes back sourced through our tools and Cala.
101	
102	| Tool | Input | Returns |
103	| --- | --- | --- |
104	| `resolve_company` | name | Cala entity: ID, sector, stage, location |
105	| `find_competitors` | company ID | 10–15 direct competitors, with a reason each |
106	| `get_rounds` | company ID | Rounds: date, amount, investors, lead flag, source |
107	| `investor_profile` | investor ID | Recent leads, sectors, stages, last activity |
108	| `check_conflict` | investor ID + company ID | Conflict yes/no, the competitor(s), sources |
109	| `rank_investors` | company ID | Scored investor list plus the "don't pitch" list |
110	| `investor_brief` | investor ID + company ID | One-page sourced brief (markdown) |
111	
112	**Stretch goal:** a follow-up chat on the results page ("What else has Fund X led in fintech this year?"), where an agent calls these tools plus Cala's own MCP.
113	
114	## Implementation: three parallel workstreams
115	
116	**Each person owns separate folders and works against shared contracts and fixtures, so nobody waits on anyone or edits the same file.** The contracts are written together on Friday night (about 1 hour) and then frozen.
117	
118	### Rules
119	
120	1. **Folder ownership.** You only commit inside your own folders. Need something changed elsewhere? Ask the owner.
121	2. **Contracts are frozen after Friday night.** `contracts/` changes only when all three agree; bump `CONTRACT_VERSION` and post in the team chat.
122	3. **Fixtures are the shared truth.** Real Cala responses recorded Friday night, saved as JSON in `contracts/fixtures/`. B builds against `FakeDataStore` (reads fixtures); C builds against a mock API that serves fixture-based responses.
123	4. **Branch per person, small PRs, merge often.** Since folders don't overlap, merges are trivial.
124	5. **Secrets.** `.env.example` is owned by A. Never commit keys (Cala, Gemini, Atlas, Verda).
125	
126	### Repo layout and owners
127	
128	```text
129	pitchlist/
130	  contracts/            ALL (frozen)  schemas.py, api.md, fixtures/*.json
131	  backend/
132	    data/               A   cala_client.py, store.py (DataStore), fake_store.py, parsers.py
133	    cache/              A   atlas.py, vector.py
134	    batch/              A   precompute_graph.py (Verda batch job)
135	    core/               B   competitors.py, conflict.py, scoring.py, briefs.py
136	    agent/              B   gemini_agent.py, tools.py, prompts/
137	    mcp_server/         B   server.py
138	    api/                B   main.py (FastAPI routes, thin)
139	    tests/              each person tests their own folder
140	  frontend/             C   Next.js app, mock/ (mock API)
141	  deploy/               A   Dockerfile, verda setup, .env.example
142	  docs/                 C   README, demo script, architecture notes
143	```
144	
145	### Contract 1: data models (`contracts/schemas.py`)
146	
147	Every fact carries its sources. Amounts stay as text (Cala returns "\~€15M"), with an optional parsed number.
148	
149	```python
150	class Source(BaseModel): name: str; url: str | None; date: str | None; rank: Literal["PRIMARY","FILING","PRESS","AGGREGATOR","UNKNOWN"]
151	class EntityRef(BaseModel): id: str; name: str; type: str; description: str | None
152	class Company(EntityRef): industries: list[str]; stage: str | None; country: str | None; total_funding_text: str | None; sources: list[Source]
153	class RoundInvestor(BaseModel): investor: EntityRef; is_lead: bool | None
154	class Round(BaseModel): id: str; company_id: str; label: str | None; date: str | None; amount_text: str | None; amount_eur: float | None; investors: list[RoundInvestor]; sources: list[Source]
155	class PortfolioLink(BaseModel): investor_id: str; company: EntityRef; sources: list[Source]
156	class PersonLink(BaseModel): person: EntityRef; company_id: str; role: Literal["BOARD","FOUNDER","CEO","EMPLOYEE"]; sources: list[Source]
157	class Competitor(BaseModel): company: Company; reason: str; similarity: float | None
158	class Conflict(BaseModel): kind: Literal["PORTFOLIO","BOARD"]; competitor: EntityRef; via_person: EntityRef | None; sources: list[Source]
159	class Reason(BaseModel): text: str; sources: list[Source]
160	class InvestorScore(BaseModel): investor: EntityRef; score: float; conflict: Conflict | None; leads_in_space: int; rounds_in_space: int; last_lead_date: str | None; warm_paths: list[Reason]; reasons: list[Reason]
161	class FounderReport(BaseModel): company: Company; competitors: list[Competitor]; pitch: list[InvestorScore]; skip: list[InvestorScore]
162	class InvestorCheck(BaseModel): investor: EntityRef; company: Company; conflicts: list[Conflict]; competitors: list[Competitor]; rounds: list[Round]
163	class Brief(BaseModel): investor_id: str; company_id: str; markdown: str; citations: list[Source]
164	```
165	
166	### Contract 2: data layer interface (A provides, B consumes)
167	
168	```python
169	class DataStore(Protocol):
170	    def resolve(self, name: str, kind: Literal["company","investor"]) -> list[EntityRef]
171	    def company(self, id: str) -> Company
172	    def rounds(self, company_id: str) -> list[Round]
173	    def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]
174	    def portfolio(self, investor_id: str) -> list[PortfolioLink]
175	    def people(self, company_id: str) -> list[PersonLink]
176	    def candidate_competitors(self, company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Company]   # vector search + knowledge_query
177	    def co_investors(self, investor_id: str) -> list[tuple[EntityRef, int]]         # from precomputed graph
178	    def sourced_answer(self, question: str) -> tuple[str, list[Source]]             # knowledge_search
179	```
180	
181	### Contract 3: REST API (B provides, C consumes)
182	
183	| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
184	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
185	| POST | `/api/resolve` | `{name, kind}` | `EntityRef[]` |
186	| POST | `/api/founder/analyze` | `{company_id}` | `FounderReport` |
187	| POST | `/api/investor/check` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `InvestorCheck` |
188	| POST | `/api/brief` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `Brief` |
189	| POST | `/api/slush-prep` | `{company_id, investor_names[]}` | `{job_id}` |
190	| GET | `/api/jobs/{id}/stream` | — | Server-sent events: agent steps, then `Brief[]` |
191	| POST | `/api/chat` | `{company_id?, investor_id?, message}` | Streamed text plus citations |
192	
193	### Workstream A — Data & infra
194	
195	**Owns:** `backend/data`, `backend/cache`, `backend/batch`, `deploy`. **Delivers:** a `DataStore` that returns contract models from real Cala data, fast and cached.
196	
197	**Friday night (first, everyone depends on it)**
198	
199	- [ ] Record fixtures: run 5 demo companies and \~10 investors through Cala; save raw responses to `contracts/fixtures/` (needs to include one counter-drone set, e.g. Sensofusion, Stendr, Nordic Air Defence)
200	- [ ] `fake_store.py`: `FakeDataStore` that returns contract models built from the fixtures, handed to B
201	
202	**Saturday**
203	
204	- [ ] `cala_client.py`: async REST client (`X-API-KEY`), retries, concurrency limit, logging of credit use
205	- [ ] `entity_introspection` once per entity type → a cached map of available fields and relationships
206	- [ ] `store.py`: real `DataStore`; every method maps Cala JSON → contract models, keeping `sources` (name, URL, date, `source_rank`)

209	- [ ] `cache/atlas.py`: cache every Cala response by entity ID plus query hash, with a 24 h TTL
210	- [ ] `cache/vector.py`: embed company descriptions (Verda Inference API); Atlas Vector Search index; `candidate_competitors()` = vector neighbours merged with a `knowledge_query` on industry + country + stage
211	
212	**Saturday night**
213	
214	- [ ] `batch/precompute_graph.py` as a Verda batch job: list active Nordic and Baltic investors → portfolios + rounds → store the co-investor edges, last-lead dates and embeddings in Atlas
215	- [ ] `co_investors()` reads the precomputed graph
216	- [ ] Deploy the backend + MCP server to a Verda CPU instance (Dockerfile, env vars, HTTPS)
217	
218	**Sunday morning:** pre-cache the 3 demo companies, check the deploy is stable, write deploy notes for the docs.
219	
220	### Workstream B — Intelligence
221	
222	**Owns:** `backend/core`, `backend/agent`, `backend/mcp_server`, `backend/api`. **Delivers:** the logic and the API, built on `FakeDataStore` until A's real store is ready (swapping it in is one line).
223	
224	**Saturday**
225	
226	- [ ] `core/competitors.py`: Gemini (Flash-tier, structured JSON output) reads the candidates and returns 10–15 `Competitor`s, with a reason for each
227	- [ ] `core/conflict.py`: PORTFOLIO conflict (an investor's `portfolio()` intersects the competitor set); BOARD conflict (an investor's people are `BOARD` on a competitor, via `people()`)
228	- [ ] `core/scoring.py`: plain-code score from leads in your space, recency of last lead, and warm paths (`co_investors()` overlap with your current investors); conflict → the skip list. Every reason carries its sources
229	- [ ] `api/main.py`: FastAPI routes exactly per Contract 3; resolve, founder/analyze and investor/check first

233	
234	- [ ] `core/briefs.py`: one `knowledge_search` per investor–company pair; keep its `explainability` claims and references as citations; Gemini only formats them into one page, adding no new facts
235	- [ ] `agent/gemini_agent.py`: function-calling loop over `agent/tools.py` (our core functions + Cala search); powers `/api/slush-prep` (plans the calls for a pasted investor list and streams each step) and `/api/chat`

241	
242	**Owns:** `frontend`, `docs`. **Delivers:** the app people use, the demo and the story. Builds against `frontend/mock/` (fixture-based responses in the Contract 3 shapes) until B's API is up; switching over is one env var (`API_URL`).

246	- [ ] Next.js scaffold, mock API from fixtures, TypeScript types mirroring `contracts/schemas.py`

250	- [ ] Home: "I'm raising / I'm investing" toggle; company (or fund + startup) input → `/api/resolve` → confirm the right entity
251	- [ ] Founder report: competitor chips (removable), a ranked **Pitch** list and a **Skip** list with the conflict reason up front
252	- [ ] Source badges on every claim: rank (Primary / Filing / Press / Aggregator) + date, with a click-through link
253	- [ ] Investor brief page (markdown + citations)
